title: Quasi-compactness and separation of spaces are etale local on the target
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $\{Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be a jointly surjective family of etale maps from schemes. Write $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ for the base changes. A morphism $g:X'\to Y'$ of algebraic spaces is called quasi-compact if for every affine scheme $Z$ and every map $h_Z\to Y'$ the algebraic space $X'\times_{Y'}Z$ is quasi-compact, meaning that it admits a surjective etale map $h_U\to X'\times_{Y'}Z$ from a quasi-compact scheme $U$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and separated if its representable diagonal is a closed immersion, meaning that each scheme test is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $f$ is quasi-compact and separated if and only if every $f_i$ is quasi-compact and separated. For scheme morphisms these properties agree with [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism].
